clue.text: Japanese clobber North Korean, apropos of nothing

parts.note: Kim is the family name of North Korea's ruling dynasty
apropos means concerning, as does 'on' (a talk on birds)
nothing is zero, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A random aside about a North Korean wearing Japanese gear, mentioned out of the blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clobber' is British slang for clothes or gear, so 'Japanese clobber' is a Japanese garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional wide-sleeved Japanese robe is a garment, and clobber is British slang for clothing.

clue.text: After change of leaders plebs prepare to root out scandal

indicators.note: the opening letters of the two words are exchanged, a leader being a first letter

parts.note: the ruck is the common mass of ordinary people
to make a meal is to prepare it

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk, roused by new leaders, get ready to dig into a scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of leaders' swaps the first letters of RUCK and MAKE, giving MUCK and RAKE.
explanation.definitionFit: To muckrake is to search out and publicise scandal about public figures, as a crusading journalist does.

clue.text: Tot escorted off

parts.note: to tot up is to add
someone escorted was led

explanation.surface: A small child was taken away by an escort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tot' looks like a toddler but is the verb to add up.
explanation.definitionFit: An addled egg is a rotten one, so the word can mean gone bad, like food that is off.

clue.text: Resistant to change, try ignoring case of piles

parts.note: to have a stab is to have a try

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outer pair of letters, so these are dropped from piles

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly set in their ways is told to attempt a remedy without bothering about haemorrhoids.
explanation.definitionFit: Stabile is a formal adjective meaning fixed, stable and not easily changed.

clue.text: Dog straying — how sad

indicators.note: letters that stray wander from their places, so these are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lament over a lost dog wandering the streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog' is the verb, to follow closely.
explanation.definitionFit: To dog someone is to follow them persistently, just as a tail or follower does.

clue.text: Elders perhaps protect sisters after small hassles

indicators.note: the larger piece comes after the S in the answer

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

indicators.note: the trees protect, so surround, the abbreviation for sisters

parts.note: elders are a kind of tree, so 'perhaps' marks an example
SS is an abbreviation for sisters

explanation.surface: Church elders shield the nuns after minor troubles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elders' suggests senior people but means elder trees.
explanation.definitionFit: Stresses as a noun are pressures and worries, the same everyday sense as hassles.

clue.text: In arrears, welcoming one pound to cash in

indicators.note: the late payment takes in, so contains, the other pieces

parts.note: a payment in arrears is late
I is the Roman numeral one
quid is British slang for a pound sterling

explanation.surface: Someone behind on payments takes in a pound so they can cash out.
explanation.definitionFit: To liquidate assets is to convert them into money, which is what cashing in means.

clue.text: Tea and scones at last, following tense conversations

indicators.note: the last letter of scones comes after the abbreviation for tense

parts.note: cha is a slang word for tea
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

indicators.note: only the final letter of scones is taken

explanation.surface: After a tense moment, tea and scones are served.
explanation.definitionFit: Chats are informal talks, so they are conversations of a light kind.

clue.text: Hollow black-framed spectacles suit groups of readers

indicators.note: the outer letters of black frame, so surround, the spectacles
a hollow word has its insides removed, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: OO looks like a pair of round spectacles
clubs are one of the four suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A pair of black-rimmed glasses goes with a suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Book clubs are societies whose members read and discuss the same books together.

clue.text: More unusual female ducks feed on farm

indicators.note: to duck is to dodge out of the way, so the letter for female drops out

parts.note: fodder is food for farm animals

explanation.surface: Hen ducks being fed in a farmyard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ducks' reads as birds but is the verb: F ducks out of FODDER.
explanation.definitionFit: Odder is the comparative of odd, meaning stranger or more peculiar.

clue.text: Upset when ringing British bird

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the whole is read backwards
the word for when encircles the abbreviation, as a ring surrounds a finger

parts.note: as can mean when (as I left)
UK is short for the United Kingdom, Britain

explanation.surface: Someone gets upset when a British bird rings them.
explanation.definitionFit: A skua is a large predatory seabird of northern waters, so it is a kind of bird.

clue.text: Stiff paper boxes that hurt chicken

indicators.note: the card boxes, so encloses, the cry of pain

parts.note: card is stiff paper
ow is what you say when something hurts

explanation.surface: Someone scared of being cut by cardboard boxes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chicken' is slang for someone timid, not the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A chicken in slang is someone lacking courage, a person who is easily scared.

clue.text: Liberal president, sensible too

parts.note: Ike was the nickname of US president Dwight Eisenhower
wise means sensible

explanation.surface: A political portrait: the president is liberal and also sensible.
explanation.definitionFit: The adverb means also or in the same way, just as too does at the end of a sentence.

clue.text: Poor soul in refuge starts to overcome troubles

parts.note: a haven is a place of refuge

indicators.note: the first letters of the next two words are taken

explanation.surface: A poor person in a shelter begins to get over hardships.
explanation.definitionFit: A have-not is someone without wealth or possessions, a poor person.

clue.text: Unlike the rest, I play-act outrageously

indicators.note: an outrageous performance is wild and disorderly, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An actor admits to hamming it up more than the rest of the cast.
explanation.definitionFit: Something atypical is not representative of its kind, differing from all the others.

clue.text: Regularly do drugs before end of very wild party

indicators.note: the picked letters come before the final letter
regularly picks every other letter, here the second, fourth and sixth
only the last letter of very is used

explanation.surface: Taking drugs habitually before a very wild party.
explanation.definitionFit: An orgy is a riotous, unrestrained party of excess, so a wild party.

clue.text: Louche servicemen pout, perhaps

parts.note: the RAF is the Royal Air Force, so airmen
the pout is a small sea fish, so an example of a fish

explanation.surface: Disreputable airmen sulking, maybe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pout' reads as a sulky face but is a fish of the cod family.
explanation.definitionFit: Raffish means disreputable but attractively so, which is what louche suggests.

clue.text: Touched gender-fluid fellow setter, making advance

indicators.note: the fellow and setter advance to the front, before the rearranged letters

parts.note: the setter refers to herself as I

indicators.note: fluid means not fixed, so the letters of gender flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A gender-fluid colleague of the setter touched someone while making a pass.
explanation.definitionFit: To finger something is to feel it with the fingers, so fingered means touched.

clue.text: Audiologist rang ENT nurses from elsewhere

indicators.note: to nurse is to hold close, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A hearing specialist phones the ear, nose and throat department to arrange nursing.
explanation.walkthrough: ENT is the ear, nose and throat hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: In an older sense strange means foreign, belonging to another place or country.

clue.text: Seeing 8 across OK

indicators.note: the number word lies across, so spans, the word for agreement

parts.note: the figure is read as the word for the number
OK is a way of saying yes

explanation.surface: It looks like a cross-reference to the answer at 8 across being approved.
explanation.walkthrough: '8 across' looks like a pointer to another clue, but 8 is the number and 'across' the containment signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Seeing as a noun is the faculty of sight, the power of vision.

clue.text: Offer rickety tumbrils without sides

indicators.note: a rickety cart is shaky and falling apart, so the letters are jumbled
without means lacking, so the letters for the sides are taken away from the jumble

parts.note: the sides are right and left, R and L

explanation.surface: Someone offers rickety tumbrils with no sides.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing R and L from TUMBRILS leaves TUMBIS, which 'rickety' rearranges. A tumbril was a cart that took prisoners to the guillotine.
explanation.definitionFit: To submit a proposal or entry is to put it forward, to offer it for consideration.

clue.text: Long line for food store

parts.note: to long for something is to pant for it
RY is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A long queue outside a food shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pantry is a small room or cupboard in which food is kept.

clue.text: Peers ultimately support minister

parts.note: to peer nosily is to pry

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of support

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords end up backing a government minister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' reads as lords but is the verb, to peer or pry.
explanation.definitionFit: A minister of religion is a clergyman, which is what a priest is.

clue.text: Bottom with extremely loathsome wrinkle

parts.note: the rump is the bottom or backside

indicators.note: the extremes of loathsome are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: An unpleasant backside with wrinkles.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumple fabric is to crease it, so the word is a verb meaning wrinkle.

clue.text: Perhaps arm Oman's leader in uncertain situation

parts.note: an arm is an example of a limb

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter of Oman's

explanation.surface: A political drama: Oman's ruler is left uncertain, perhaps through armed action.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in limbo is being in an unresolved, in-between state, waiting with no decision.

clue.text: Time to prepare ready-mix stuffing

indicators.note: to prepare a mix is to work it into shape, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: It's time to make up the ready-made stuffing for the roast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stuffing' looks like the food but means stuffing animal skins.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermy is the craft of preserving and mounting animal skins, filling them so they look alive.

clue.text: Buyers' representatives refuse to go into this hut

parts.note: CA is the Consumers' Association, which represents shoppers in Britain
a bin is the container rubbish is put into

explanation.surface: Shoppers' advocates decline to enter a shack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' looks like the verb to decline but is the noun for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cabin is a small, simple wooden house, much like a hut.

clue.text: Outside layers, inside then outside layers

parts.note: the egg is what lies inside a shell
shells are the hard outer layers of eggs

explanation.surface: A puzzle about layers within layers, described from the outside in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Layers' also hints at hens: the egg is the inside, then come the shells outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Eggshells are the hard coverings of eggs, an outer layer around them.
